nodes.label: ICRR Mark (2x2 Quadrant Monogram)
nodes.rationale: Standalone square brand mark: a 1000x1000 four-quadrant checkerboard spelling I / C / R / R in a high-contrast Didone-style serif. Square aspect and no wordmark make it the favicon / avatar / app-icon asset, legible at small sizes where the full journal name would collapse.

nodes.label: Four-Quadrant Checkerboard Monogram
nodes.rationale: The acronym is laid out as a 2x2 grid rather than a single line so the mark reads as a square. Reading order is left-to-right, top-to-bottom (I C / R R). The grid also evokes a bound page or a quadrant of a journal cover, keeping the academic register without literal book imagery.

nodes.label: Diagonal Reversed-Contrast Tile Pairing
nodes.rationale: Tiles alternate on the diagonal: top-left and bottom-right are oxblood ground with bone letterforms, top-right and bottom-left are bone ground with oxblood letterforms. The alternation is what makes the grid legible without any drawn gridlines - the color swap itself is the divider - and it guarantees every letter keeps a high contrast ratio against its own tile.

nodes.label: Oxblood + Bone Two-Color Palette
nodes.rationale: Deep oxblood/maroon (approx #5E1F22) against a warm bone off-white (approx #F5F1EC). Strictly two brand colors, no gradients or tints, so the identity survives one-color print, embossing and small-size rendering. The warm off-white avoids the clinical feel of pure #FFFFFF and signals paper stock.

nodes.label: Transparent-Background Asset Convention
nodes.rationale: Both lockups ship with alpha transparency (the _transparent filename suffix) so they can sit on any page background; the bone tiles inside the mark stay opaque, meaning the mark itself always carries its own light ground and never inverts incorrectly on a dark surface.

nodes.label: Horizontal / Stacked / Mark-Only Variant System
nodes.rationale: Three assets cover three aspect-ratio budgets rather than one asset being scaled: wide horizontal for headers, stacked for covers and narrow viewports, bare mark for favicons and avatars. Choosing by available space instead of by scaling keeps the wordmark's letterspaced caps above their legibility floor in every context.
